PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

12.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Jimenez provided an overview of the past two weeks. Regarding loitering concerns on Watcher Street, he reported that deputies reached out to residents, increased patrols, and installed surveillance cameras. No further incidents have been reported since. Councilmember Garcia thanked Sergeant Jimenez for addressing the issue, noting that residents were also appreciative. 
Mayor Pro Tem Lainez stated that the Fourth of July event went smoothly without any issues and thanked the deputies for their support.

Mayor Altamirano expressed appreciation to Joseph McLellan, a probation officer, and noted that he had the opportunity to tour Juvenile Hall.

Probation Officer Joseph McLellan gave a presentation on his role, sharing that there are currently 1,000 active probation cases. His responsibilities include monitoring gang activity, conducting compliance checks, making phone calls, visiting schools, and providing outreach.

Councilmember Garcia requested a comparison of current probation statistics with those from the previous year to track changes in the number of individuals on probation.

11.. Appeal of the Planning Commission’s Decision to Approve Conditional Use Permit No. 25-02 to Allow a Hotel Use in the City’s Unlimited Commercial (“C-2”) Zoning District at 500 Citadel Drive, Commerce  -  Action: adopt (Pass) City Attorney Tapia explained that this item is an appeal, which was previously placed on the agenda at the last meeting, during which the public hearing was opened. He noted that staff would provide a presentation, followed by comments from the applicant, the appellant, and members of the public.

Community Development Director Jessica Serrano provided an overview of the staff report. Mayor Pro Tem Lainez inquired about the supporting documentation and the project timeline. Director Serrano clarified that the documentation included a letter from the applicant's attorney explaining why the project qualifies for a Class 1 Categorical Exemption under CEQA, along with a vehicle trip study. The study concluded that the proposed hotel would generate fewer trips than the existing office use.

Steve Craig, the applicant, stated that the building has already been constructed, and they are now proceeding with tenant improvements. The anticipated timeline to open the hotel is approximately nine months. He emphasized that the project is 100% privately funded, environmentally responsible, and will create visibility and economic benefits for the community. He projected over $1 million in new annual revenue for the City and stated that Commerce residents would be prioritized for employment opportunities. He also mentioned that the project has received strong community support, with over 500 resident signatures collected in favor.
Jordan Sissun, representing Unite Here Local 11, expressed concerns that the staff report did not adequately address environmental impacts. He asserted that the project does not qualify for a CEQA exemption due to the major operational changes, which include different impacts on energy, water usage, and traffic. He also challenged the validity of the vehicle trip study, claiming the assumptions were unsustainable.

Martha Martinez spoke in opposition and urged the Council to require a full CEQA review, citing the proposed change as a significant land use shift.


Page Gosney, land use counsel representing the appellant, stated that repurposing the building triggers new environmental impacts and argued that the Class 1 exemption does not apply. He reiterated the need for a CEQA review and criticized the traffic study as flawed.

Alejandro Martinez and Jose Calderon, also representing Unite Here Local 11, asked the Council to uphold the appeal and raised concerns regarding the Vehicle Miles Traveled (VMT) analysis.

Tim Flaming, the project architect, emphasized their firm’s experience in hospitality and retail design. He highlighted the Citadel’s national reputation and the economic benefits of converting the building, including job creation and increased transient occupancy tax revenue for the City.

Jonathan Chambers addressed traffic concerns, stating that the project would generate fewer trips than the previous office use, resulting in less than significant impact. He added that VMT analysis is not required and noted that tour groups and shuttle services would reduce individual vehicle use, as visitors would stay at the hotel rather than travel back and forth.

City Attorney Tapia noted that the City received a letter from Page Gosney dated July 7, 2025, which was included in the record and distributed to the City Council, along with a report from Smart Mobility dated the same day.

Mayor Argumedo thanked the applicant and Unite Here Local 11 representatives for their input. He expressed his view that there is no legal or procedural basis to prevent the project from moving forward.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS There were no Council reports.
